name: Timothy Bloodworth
bio: a Delegate, a Representative, and a Senator from North Carolina; born in New Hanover County, N.C., in 1736; teacher; served in the Revolutionary War; in 1776 was employed in making muskets and bayonets for the Continental Army; member, North Carolina state house of commons 1778-1779; treasurer of Wilmington District 1781-1782; appointed commissioner of confiscated property in 1783; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1786; member, North Carolina state senate 1788-1789; elected to the First Congress and served from April 6, 1790, to March 3, 1791; member, North Carolina state house of representatives 1793-1794; elected to the United States Senate and served from March 4, 1795, to March 3, 1801; collector of customs at Wilmington; died in Wilmington, N.C., August 24, 1814.
